record.paper_title: Stability of Homomorphisms, Coverings and Cocycles II: Examples, Applications and Open Problems
record.original_question: Find a family of finite groups G with presentations G ≅ <S|R> such that the presentations are short in the sense that the numbers of generators and relations are polylogarithmic in |G| and every relation has polylogarithmic length in |G|, while the stability rate is still strong enough that the presentation is ρ-stable with ρ(ε) = polyloglog(|G|) · ε^c for some constant c > 0 independent of |G|.

evidence.quote:
Problem 6.9 (Efficient stability in permutations). Find a family of finite groups {G}, with presentations
G ∼= hS|Ri, such that:
• The presentation is (somewhat) short:
|S|, |R| = polylog(|G|)
∀r ∈ R : |r| = polylog(|G|).
• The stability rate is good: hS|Ri is ρ-stable, and ρ(ε) = polyloglog(|G|) · εc for some c > 0 independent
of |G|.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Let $G$ be a finite group and let $\langle S \mid R\rangle$ be a finite presentation of $G$, where $S$ is a finite generating set and $R$ is a finite set of relations (words in the free group $F(S)$). For a word $r\in F(S)$, write $|r|$ for its length. For each integer $n\ge 1$ let $\mathrm{Sym}(n)$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters, equipped with the normalized Hamming distance
$$d_H(\sigma,\tau)=\frac{1}{n}\big|\{i:\sigma(i)\ne\tau(i)\}\big|.$$
A map $\varphi:S\to \mathrm{Sym}(n)$ extends uniquely to a homomorphism $\tilde\varphi:F(S)\to \mathrm{Sym}(n)$. The defect of $\varphi$ with respect to the presentation $\langle S\mid R\rangle$ is
$$\mathrm{def}(\varphi)=\max_{r\in R} d_H(\tilde\varphi(r),\mathrm{id}).$$
The distance from $\varphi$ to a genuine homomorphism is
$$\mathrm{dist}(\varphi,\mathrm{Hom}(G,\mathrm{Sym}(n)))=\inf_{\psi:G\to\mathrm{Sym}(n)\ \text{hom.}}\ \max_{s\in S} d_H(\varphi(s),\psi(s)).$$
Given a function $\rho:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ with $\rho(0)=0$ and $\rho$ continuous at $0$, the presentation $\langle S\mid R\rangle$ is called $\rho$-stable (in permutations) if for every $n\ge 1$ and every $\varphi:S\to\mathrm{Sym}(n)$,
$$\mathrm{dist}(\varphi,\mathrm{Hom}(G,\mathrm{Sym}(n)))\ \le\ \rho(\mathrm{def}(\varphi)).$$

Problem. Exhibit an infinite family of finite groups $\{G\}$ together with presentations $G\cong\langle S\mid R\rangle$ satisfying both of the following simultaneously:

(i) The presentations are short, in the sense that
$$|S|,\ |R|\ =\ \mathrm{polylog}(|G|)\quad\text{and}\quad |r|=\mathrm{polylog}(|G|)\ \text{for every }r\in R.$$

(ii) The stability rate is good: each presentation $\langle S\mid R\rangle$ is $\rho$-stable with
$$\rho(\varepsilon)\ =\ \mathrm{polyloglog}(|G|)\cdot \varepsilon^{c}$$
for some constant $c>0$ that does not depend on $|G|$.

Either construct such a family or prove no such family exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a 2023 survey on stability of homomorphisms, coverings and cocycles. Recent works on stability in permutations (e.g., constraint stability and action traces, local permutation stability) discuss qualitative stability and characterizations but do not exhibit families of finite groups with simultaneously polylogarithmic-size presentations and polyloglog-times-power stability rates. No resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Constraint stability in permutations and action traces
status_evidence.snippet: Provides new examples of groups stable in permutations via constraint stability and action traces, focusing on amenable groups; does not address efficient quantitative stability rates for short presentations.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on stability in permutations does not resolve the question of exhibiting short presentations with polyloglog stability rate.

status_evidence.title: Local permutation stability
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces local stability in permutations for finitely generated groups and connects it to sofic/LEF properties; not concerned with quantitative rates polyloglog(|G|)·ε^c on short presentations.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on local permutation stability does not provide the requested efficient stability family.
